title: Transaction (user-visible money-movement history row)
description: One row a user reads as their history. NOT THE SAME ENTITY AS LedgerEntry (canonical-model.md D4): a Transaction is presentation with provenance, and it may exist without any ledger counterpart (a manual entry); a LedgerEntry is the accounting fact. The amount is signed and its SIGN IS THE DIRECTION - '>= 0 is in, < 0 is out', and the zero amount counts as 'in' because that is the schema's rule, kept as written rather than second-guessed (finance/transactions DirectionOf). `hash` is nullable in the table but EXACT ON-CHAIN RECONCILIATION REQUIRES IT: rows without it are for display, not reconciliation. `source` must survive every merge. `date` is a calendar DATE, not an instant - it is the field that makes date-only ordering ambiguous (see common/time.json T3).

id.description: SQL surrogate key (INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT). There is no canonical transaction id.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD calendar date as stored (TEXT NOT NULL). Validated by transactions.New; NOT an instant, so ordering by it alone is ambiguous and callers must break ties by id.

chain.description: Free-form today; the Go default is 'Offchain'. chain_id joins it once chain ids exist.

event.description: The event label shown to the user; required non-empty by the table.

amount_usd.description: SIGNED: its sign IS the direction. Null (unreported) must never be read as 0.

direction.description: Must agree with amount_usd's sign; derived from it when absent, never contradicted.

hash.description: Chain transaction hash. REQUIRED for exact reconciliation; null means display-only.

source.description: Provenance ('manual' is the default). Survives every operation and is never dropped by a merge.

recorded_at.description: SQL created_at. LEGACY ENCODING is text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', not integer ms.
